top_categories.workout_context: 123ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Colnago Gran Fondo Mont Ventoux, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Colnago Gran Fondo Mont Ventoux. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 84 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Colnago Gran Fondo Mont Ventoux's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
10,318ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
10,318ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Colnago Gran Fondo Mont Ventoux. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 84, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Colnago Gran Fondo Mont Ventoux. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 10,318ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 84 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
